<thought>We have a molecular ion at m/z ≈ 199.000, which matches the monoisotopic mass of C₈H₁₀BrN (exact mass = 198.99966). The ¹³C NMR shows eight distinct carbons: six aromatic signals (≈ 121–139 ppm) and two aliphatic signals (≈ 38–44 ppm), consistent with a brominated phenethylamine (a benzene ring bearing Br and a –CH₂–CH₂–NH₂ side chain). The SMILES “CCNCC1=CC=C(C=C1)Br” encodes this structure and yields the correct formula. Therefore the required SMILES string is:

**CCNCC1=CC=C(C=C1)Br**</thought>
